data.one_liner: A simple widget for having child widgets that respond to gestures with a spring animation.
data.what_it_does: SpringButton wraps a child widget and extends functionality similar to a GestureDetector, adding spring physics animations upon user interaction. It supports multiple gesture callbacks and customization parameters like scale coefficient and duration.
use_when: You want child widgets or buttons to give physical spring-like feedback upon touch gestures.
You need a drop-in replacement for GestureDetector that includes built-in spring animations.
avoid_when: You need complex physics-based multi-element animations handled via Rive or full game engines.
You need complex declarative page transitions.
strengths: Familiar API closely mirroring standard Flutter GestureDetector.
Supports null safety and a wide range of gesture callbacks.
weaknesses: Limited to spring scaling animations on touch rather than arbitrary physics-based motion.
Author notes it was built early in their Flutter learning journey.

alternatives.name: flutter_animate
alternatives.why_pick_it: For general-purpose declarative animations and effects applied to widgets.

alternatives.name: rive
alternatives.why_pick_it: For advanced interactive vector animations and rich motion graphics.

data.minimal_example:
SpringButton(
    SpringButtonType.OnlyScale,
    uiChild(),
    scaleCoefficient: 0.75,
    duration: 1000,
    onTap: () {},
)
